note: D18 final (V1 side): three-level downstream eval, V1 rx-only K=4 lr=5e-4 --shuffle seed=42. delta = MoE - Vanilla, same downstream training for both.
verdict: The upstream rx-only MoE advantage does NOT transfer. Mean delta -0.00445 over 112 (scenario, usage) pairs, t=-2.72. ModuleUsage is the worst hit (-0.0137): handing the MoE Cross layers directly to a downstream model is actively harmful. Only 4 of 14 usage methods are positive on average.
implication: Scope the headline strictly to upstream parameter efficiency. The rx-only regime buys cheap upstream AUC, not better transferable representations — plausibly because freezing the embedding table forces the Cross experts to absorb scenario-specific signal that does not generalise. D19 tests this by re-running downstream under full and partial freeze regimes.
